steps.name: QC and outlier characterization
steps.question: How much does sample_03 deviate from the other 4 control (or treated) samples in the counts.csv matrix, and is its deviation consistent with a technical artifact (library size, gene detection rate) or a biological outlier?
acceptance_criteria: Reports sample_03's group assignment (treated or control) from metadata.csv
Reports library size, number of detected genes, and PCA/hierarchical-clustering distance of sample_03 relative to its group's centroid and to the other group
Reports whether sample_03's deviation pattern looks technical (e.g., low depth, high proportion of low-count genes) or biological (e.g., high expression of markers concordant with treatment)
Produces a PCA plot and sample-distance heatmap with sample_03 labeled, confirming or refining the caveat already noted in the data profile

steps.name: Primary DE: treated vs control, all 10 samples
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between the 5 treated and 5 control samples in counts.csv, using all 10 samples including sample_03?
acceptance_criteria: Uses DESeq2 (or equivalent negative-binomial model) on raw integer counts with condition (treated vs control) as the design
Reports Cook's distance / influence diagnostics per sample-gene combination and flags whether sample_03 drives an outsized share of the significant hits
Outputs a full results table (log2FoldChange, p-value, BH-adjusted p-value) for all ~12000 genes
Reports the count of genes at padj < 0.05 and |log2FC| > 1

steps.name: Sensitivity DE: treated vs control, sample_03 excluded
steps.question: Which genes are differentially expressed between treated and control when sample_03 is excluded (4 vs 5, or 4 vs 4 depending on its group), and how does this gene list compare to the all-samples result?
acceptance_criteria: Re-runs the same DESeq2 design after removing sample_03 from counts.csv/metadata.csv
Reports the resulting group sizes explicitly (e.g., 4 vs 5)
Outputs a full results table for comparison
Quantifies overlap (Jaccard or simple count) between the significant gene sets from T1S2 and this run, and reports genes that are significant only when sample_03 is included
States plainly whether conclusions about treated-vs-control DE are sensitive to sample_03's inclusion

steps.name: Pathway enrichment of primary DE gene list
steps.question: Which WikiPathways human pathways are enriched among genes differentially expressed between treated and control (from the all-samples DE result, T1S2), and do the same pathways come out of the sample_03-excluded list (T1S3)?
acceptance_criteria: Uses the WikiPathways human GMT gene sets (HGNC symbols) confirmed present in the reference store for enrichment
Runs enrichment (e.g., over-representation or GSEA-style ranked test) on the significant gene list from T1S2, and separately on T1S3, using the full detected gene list as background
Reports enriched pathways with adjusted p-values, and flags whether top pathways differ between the all-samples and sample_03-excluded runs
If the WikiPathways reference is unavailable at run time, reports that gap explicitly rather than fabricating pathway results

plan.title: Treated vs control DE with outlier-sensitivity check
plan.analytical_narrative: The dataset is bulk RNA-seq (Salmon gene-level counts, 12000 genes x 10 samples) with a simple 5-vs-5 treated/control design, unpaired, single batch. The data context flags sample_03 as separating from the rest of its group on PCA and the sample-distance heatmap — this is a QC caveat, not a resolved decision, so the plan does not silently drop sample_03. Instead it runs the differential expression analysis twice (all 10 samples, and with sample_03 excluded), compares the two gene lists, and lets the DE step itself quantify sample_03's leverage (Cook's distance / influence diagnostics) before any exclusion decision is treated as final. This avoids two failure modes: ignoring a possible technical outlier that inflates variance and hides real signal, and silently excluding a sample that may be a genuine biological responder. Downstream, the significant gene list from the primary (all-samples) run is used for pathway enrichment against WikiPathways human gene sets, which are confirmed present in the reference store. All steps operate on the actual counts.csv / metadata.csv files and the actual treated vs control condition contrast.
